Facts: Heirs challenged public will of 90-year-old testator showing subsequent senile decline; notary certified capacity at execution.
Legal Framework: Article 591 Italian Civil Code requiring total incapacity to understand and will for testamentary nullity.
Interpretive Issue: Whether age-related mental decline, subsequent disability recognition, or partial cognitive impairment suffices to establish testamentary incapacity under Article 591.
Legal Principle Applied: Testamentary annulment under Article 591 Civil Code requires proof of complete deprivation of awareness and self-determination at the precise moment of will execution, not mere mental faculty alteration. Subsequent pathology or disability certification constitutes only a presumptive starting point; generic senile decline insufficient absent proof of total volitional incapacity. The notary's capacity assessment in public wills constitutes significant evidence of testator's soundness, rebuttable only through rigorous contrary proof.
